=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

## Buyer’s position

**Do not accept this package as drafted.** The Seller seeks both to transfer unresolved completion risks to Wattlebridge and to restrict the remedies available if those risks materialise. The principal concerns are conditional customer consent, outstanding secured debt, uncertain IP ownership, omitted transaction costs and limitations extending beyond ordinary warranty claims.

This review is based on the supplied update and Disclosure Letter, not the underlying DD documents or complete SPA. References to those documents are therefore evidence leads, not independently verified findings. The embedded “SYSTEM NOTE” is not a substantive deal term and has been disregarded.

## 1. Completion and price protection — highest priority

| Issue | Why the Seller’s position is adverse | Buyer pushback |
|---|---|---|
| **Bluefen consent — clauses 3 / 6.3** | Bluefen represents approximately **30% of FY26 revenue**. The Disclosure Letter expressly confirms that neither final consent nor satisfaction of associated conditions has been evidenced. Delivery of a written consent alone may leave conditions, fees or adverse contractual changes outstanding. “Reasonable endeavours” is not a completion outcome. | Require an effective written consent, with all associated conditions satisfied and no materially adverse amendments, as a **Buyer-waivable condition precedent**. Review clauses 11.2–11.3 and the consent itself. Require supporting evidence, a long-stop date and termination rights if unsatisfied. |
| **Riverlark debt and security — clauses 2 / 7** | Approximately **$3.2m remains outstanding**. A release promised after Completion leaves the acquired company exposed to debt, security enforcement and change-of-control consequences. That is inconsistent with the debt-free/cash-free baseline unless properly addressed through price and closing mechanics. | Obtain a current payout letter covering principal, interest, fees and all secured obligations; pay the lender directly through Completion funds flow; and require effective release arrangements at Completion. Any later administrative deregistration should be backed by binding lender undertakings and prompt follow-up. Deduct the debt from Seller proceeds under the agreed price mechanism, **without double counting**. |
| **Completion bonuses — $420,000 plus possible on-costs** | Their omission from funds flow does not make them economically irrelevant. If Paperbark pays after acquisition, the Buyer may bear a sale-triggered liability while the Seller receives an unadjusted price. Continued-employment conditions also require careful allocation. | Agree expressly who bears the bonuses and associated payroll tax, superannuation and other applicable on-costs. Buyer’s opening position: Seller-funded sale-triggered costs, reflected in funds flow, a debt-like adjustment or a specific indemnity. Check individual terms and payment timing; distinguish genuine post-Completion retention arrangements negotiated by Buyer. |
| **Share title — DD-012** | A register naming Harbourglass is relevant but does not alone establish unencumbered title, valid issuance, the absence of competing rights or a fully diluted 100% acquisition. | Verify issued capital, beneficial ownership, options/convertibles, pre-emption rights, encumbrances and transfer restrictions. Require all necessary approvals, executed transfers and registration steps, plus robust title and capacity warranties. Do not accept an acknowledgement that Buyer has verified title merely because the register was provided. |

**Key distinction:** an indemnity is not an adequate substitute for securing a critical customer consent, obtaining clear title or releasing lender security at Completion.

## 2. The liability regime needs structural changes

### General cap and thresholds

The proposed **20% cap ($4.8m)** is a negotiation point, not something to accept as inherently “standard”. Its adequacy depends on the warranties, diligence findings, exclusions, claim periods and Seller’s ability to pay.

The thresholds materially erode recovery:

- The **$25,000 de minimis** can exclude numerous smaller losses.
- The **$250,000 deductible basket** leaves Buyer bearing the first $250,000 even once qualifying claims exceed it.
- “Exceeds” creates strict cut-offs; clarify treatment of claims exactly at the threshold.

**Pushback:** seek a higher general cap, lower thresholds and a tipping basket rather than an excess-only basket. Require related claims arising from the same facts or cause to aggregate, and state clearly how qualifying claims count towards the basket. Thresholds should not automatically apply to fundamental warranties, tax protections, specific indemnities or payment obligations.

### Fundamental warranties must not share the general regime

Capacity and title are central to whether Buyer receives what it pays for. “Administrative simplicity” is not a commercial justification for limiting them to $4.8m and 18 months.

**Pushback:** a separate fundamental-warranty regime, with a cap at least equal to the purchase price, materially longer survival and no de minimis or basket. Define the category carefully to include authority, ownership, capitalisation and absence of share encumbrances or competing rights.

### Claim periods must match the risk

Eighteen months may be too short to identify problems through a complete reporting and audit cycle. It is particularly inappropriate as a universal deadline.

**Pushback:**

- Seek a longer general warranty period, for example **24 months**.
- Give tax claims a period aligned with relevant statutory assessment/reassessment exposure, with an appropriate buffer and treatment of extended exposure.
- Give fundamental warranties and specific indemnities separately negotiated periods.
- Ensure timely notification preserves a claim while its amount or outcome remains unresolved. Avoid unnecessarily onerous notice requirements or short proceedings deadlines that defeat otherwise valid claims.

### Reject limitations applying indiscriminately to “all Claims”

Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 13 and 20.5 could undermine specific protections by importing general caps, deadlines, exclusions and exclusive-remedy language into every cause of action.

**Pushback:** create an express hierarchy and carve-outs covering:

- Fundamental warranties.
- Tax covenant/indemnity claims.
- Specific indemnities, including Ironquay and any agreed incident indemnity.
- Purchase-price adjustments, debt repayment and other express payment obligations.
- Fraud, fraudulent concealment and deliberate misconduct, with carefully negotiated attribution.
- Rights that cannot lawfully be excluded.

Exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions must not silently neutralise these protections. Review their precise operation under NSW and applicable Commonwealth law; do not assume either that every exclusion is effective or that statutory rights will rescue poor drafting.

## 3. Disclosure and knowledge protections are too broad

### Reject blanket data-room and public-register disclosure

Disclosing everything “contained or referred to” in a data room shifts the burden of finding and interpreting risks to Buyer. It can also sweep in documents not actually supplied.

**Pushback:** disclosures should identify the nature and scope of the exception with enough detail for Buyer to understand it. Require specific warranty cross-references and a frozen, indexed, retained data-room copy. Reject general public-record disclosure, or tightly confine it to identified records and agreed searches.

Most importantly, **disclosure should not qualify conditions precedent, price mechanics, fundamental warranties or specific indemnities unless expressly agreed**. A disclosed problem still requires a negotiated allocation of its cost.

### Narrow the Buyer-knowledge exclusion

Clause 8.3 combines Buyer and adviser knowledge with anything discoverable from records. That creates constructive knowledge and could defeat claims for matters no decision-maker actually understood.

**Pushback:** delete the exclusion or limit it to actual conscious knowledge of specifically named Buyer individuals at an agreed time. Exclude deemed knowledge, adviser imputation and a duty to investigate. It should not defeat specific indemnities for known risks.

## 4. Specific diligence risks need targeted treatment

### Ironquay IP

The evidence indicates a **conditional transfer of SOW3 Project Materials**, with $180,000 recorded as open. It does **not** conclusively prove non-payment or resolve ownership.

A payment-only indemnity is insufficient: the exposure could include missing ownership rights, infringement allegations, disruption and replacement costs.

**Require:**

- Verification of payment status and the complete contractual chain of title.
- Cleared payment where required, together with confirmatory assignment/release and necessary background-IP licences.
- Completion delivery of critical ownership documents.
- A specific indemnity covering relevant pre-Completion ownership and payment defects and resulting losses—not merely the invoice amount—with appropriate separate limitations.

### Export/privacy incident

The record establishes an unintended delivery of a link and a possible export of approximately 1,240 records. It does **not** establish unauthorised access, a confirmed notifiable breach or a quantified loss. Equally, the Seller has no adequate basis to dismiss it as immaterial.

**Require:** prompt investigation and preservation of logs; confirmation of scope, access, containment and applicable legal/contractual notification requirements; Buyer visibility into material developments; and appropriate pre-Completion remediation. Seek a specific indemnity for pre-Completion incident consequences, including investigation, remediation and third-party claims, to the extent legally recoverable. Consider retention/security while exposure remains unresolved.

### Sandbar renewals — $330,000 aggregate

Neither “ordinary course” nor immediate liability is established. The three related renewals must be assessed together.

**Require:** signed terms, renewal and cancellation dates, termination rights, service periods and accounting treatment. Test aggregate commitments against interim operating covenants. Allocate amounts according to their substance: do not automatically treat future operating services as debt, but do not let the Seller exclude accrued liabilities or unusual pre-Completion commitments by labelling them ordinary course.

### Tax and broader IP warranties

These are not “settled” merely because Seller says so. Tax needs appropriately scoped warranties and a covenant/indemnity for pre-Completion tax, subject to negotiated exclusions. Review software ownership, contractor assignments, licences, open-source obligations and infringement exposure separately from Ironquay.

### Lease and Mossvale

Do **not** invent consent requirements:

- DD-007 reportedly establishes a **lease notification** obligation, not landlord consent.
- DD-009 reportedly restricts **assignment**, not necessarily a share-sale change of control.

Review the complete provisions and comply with actual requirements. Obtain consents only where legally or contractually required.

## Recommended negotiation summary

1. **Make effective Bluefen consent, secured-debt discharge and clear share title completion requirements.**
2. **Reconcile funds flow** for Riverlark, bonuses/on-costs and any agreed Ironquay payment, avoiding duplicate deductions.
3. **Replace the “all Claims” limitations** with separate regimes for general warranties, fundamentals, tax and specific indemnities.
4. **Reject blanket disclosure and constructive Buyer knowledge.**
5. **Resolve IP ownership and investigate the export incident**, with targeted indemnities and appropriate recovery security.
6. **Verify actual contractual triggers** for renewals, lease notification and Mossvale—neither accepting Seller characterisations nor overstating the evidence.
7. Check Seller covenant strength and consider escrow, retention or a guarantee: **a contractual claim is only useful if recoverable.**
